task: T-022/T-051 — Android release voice admission microphone capture crash
summary: Reproduced the Android release crash when microphone capture begins during voice admission. Flutter supplied integer sampleRate/channelCount constraints, and the Android WebRTC fork force-cast Number values to Double. The parser now converts Number.doubleValue(), so both integer and floating-point constraints are accepted.

checks.name: Initial permission-denied listener fallback
checks.observation: The first entry attempt had RECORD_AUDIO denied with USER_FIXED. The client connected as a listener and reported NotAllowedError rather than crashing; that path never reached microphone capture and could not reproduce the reported failure. Granting permission and retrying entered getUserAudio and exposed the fatal numeric cast below.

checks.name: Pre-fix Android crash reproduction
checks.observation: After granting RECORD_AUDIO and retrying microphone activation in SHARE_TEST, AndroidRuntime recorded a fatal ClassCastException (Integer cannot be cast to Double) in ConstraintsMap.getDouble → MediaConstraintsUtils → GetUserMediaImpl.getUserAudio. The app process exited; this did not originate from the APK's compressed native-library packaging.

checks.name: WebRTC numeric constraint regression
checks.observation: The focused test failed before the fix with the same ClassCastException, then passed for both Integer and Double inputs after the parser change.

checks.name: Full Flutter test suite
checks.observation: Repeated after rebasing the fix onto the latest origin/master commit.

checks.name: Android release voice-entry runtime regression
checks.observation: Installed the signed 1.0.34+67 arm64 APK in place, preserving app data/session. With RECORD_AUDIO granted, SHARE_TEST connected and published the microphone without a process crash or AndroidRuntime fatal. The microphone was immediately muted, the test room was left, and RECORD_AUDIO was revoked afterward.

checks.name: Post-test device cleanup
checks.observation: The updated APK remains installed, the emulator's RECORD_AUDIO permission is denied as before the test, and Android records the post-test process stop as PERMISSION CHANGE rather than a crash.

checks.observation: Tag android-v1.0.34 on source revision 4828557c51e5ab0da64aff5e800ab982a355709e completed the Android Release workflow successfully. limitations: The regression was reproduced on the API 35 emulator; the user's physical handset was not connected for this run.
The emulator runtime smoke test used the locally signed 1.0.34+67 build; the published GitHub release was built from the tagged source revision by CI.
